reasons: Mis-classification: the fallback position requires affiliate coverage (at minimum on written notice) plus successor transferability. Section 1.4 grants access and use rights to 'the Company' only — no affiliates, no contractors, and no notice mechanic to add them — so a material term of the fallback is unmet, and the deterministic check 'affiliates covered by the licence' correctly fails.

The rationale's key premise ('no restriction preventing the Company from having its affiliates or contractors exercise the access') is contradicted by the very paragraph it cites for the successor element: Section 10.3 states 'no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement,' which affirmatively excludes affiliates and contractors from any rights and leaves no path to add them — the rule's walk-away trigger.

Section 10.3 is a standard successors-and-assigns/binding-effect clause; it confirms the Agreement inures to successors but does not itself grant an affirmative right to transfer the licence in an M&A transaction, so it only weakly supports the second fallback element and cannot cure the missing affiliate coverage.

This should be raised as a deviation with an actionable redline (e.g., insert 'and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf' in Section 1.4, and carve affiliates/contractors out of the 'no other person' limitation in Section 10.3, offering the written-notice fallback), together with a [Playbook] comment; as filed the finding is retained as compliant evidence and the issue is never negotiated.
